Last updated November 14, 2026.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • At the recording office fees payable by cash, check, debit or credit card; card use adds 2.75% merchant fee on the entire transaction (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Jackson County by the numbers

Where is the Jackson County, MO Recorder of Deeds office?

The Recorder of Deeds works from one place only, the Historic Truman Courthouse at 112 W. Lexington, Suite 30, in Independence, MO 64050. Walk-in service runs weekdays from 8 a.m. until 5 p.m., with county holidays off. Call 816-881-4483 or write to records@jacksongov.org.

The Kansas City courthouse at 415 E. 12th St. handles tax payments, but the county states the recorder is located only in Independence. Mail submissions go to the same suite. Documents also arrive through electronic filing, which banks, title companies and law firms use, and Jackson County accepts electronic signatures and notarization through that route and at the walk-in and mail desk.

What does the recorder do for a house sale in Jackson County?

The office reviews and indexes each document before it enters the public record. It checks that the paper meets the minimum recording requirements. It does not fill out forms, help owners complete them, or check the content, so questions about wording belong with a title agent or a Missouri attorney.

The buyer's deed ends up in this office's index, and so does the lender's release after a payoff. The county says it records nearly 100 types of documents.

  • Deeds and deeds of trust
  • Releases and assignments of mortgages
  • Uniform Commercial Code real estate filings
  • State and federal tax liens and releases
  • Notices of mechanic's lien
  • Plats and surveys

What is the price of recording a deed in Jackson County?

A standard deed runs $23 on page one and $3 on each page that follows. The county posted a new fee schedule, and any document received on or after August 28, 2026 falls under it, whether it came by e-recording or by mail, regardless of postmark. That date has now passed, so the schedule below is the one in force.

Jackson County, MO recording charges on the county fee page
ServiceFee
Deed or other document, first page$23
Each additional page$3
Release or assignment, each extra affected number$5
Notice of mechanic's lien$23
State or federal tax lien$3
Tax lien release$1.50
Document copy, first page$2
Copy, each extra page$1
Certification$1 per document

Sources: Jackson County Recorder of Deeds recording fees page.

Where does a Jackson County recording fee go?

Out of the $23 first-page charge, $8 goes to the State of Missouri and $15 stays in the county. The state share is split among the Secretary of State Local Preservation Fund, the State Surveyor Fund, the State Housing Trust Fund and the State Statutory County Recorder's Fund. The county share is divided between the General Fund, the Recorder's Fee Fund, a County Homeless Fund and a Technology Fund. Each added page at $3 goes entirely to the county's General Fund.

A recording line on a settlement statement is a flat amount tied to page count, so a longer deed with exhibits costs a few dollars more.

How can I pay the Jackson County recorder?

By mail, make the check payable to the Recorder of Deeds Department. At the recording office you can pay with cash, check, debit or credit card. A debit or credit card adds a 2.75% merchant processing fee on the entire transaction, so a large batch of documents costs noticeably more by card than by check.

Certified copies of deeds can be ordered online through the county's Aumentum portal at aumentumweb.jacksongov.org. A certified marriage license copy costs $10, and a plain request by mail needs a personal check or money order for that amount.

What must a deed look like to be recorded in Jackson County?

Page one must carry the document title, its date, every grantor with marital status, every grantee, any statutory addresses and the legal description, all below a three-inch top margin. This mirrors Missouri statute 59.310, which also calls for at least three-quarters of an inch on the other sides, type no smaller than eight-point, dark ink, and white or light paper of at least twenty-pound weight.

  • Pages are printed on one side only and are not permanently bound.
  • Signatures are in dark ink with the name typed or printed beneath.
  • A document that misses the format rules can still be recorded for an extra $25 under the statute.
  • The recorder returns a rejected document with an explanation.

The county also recommends leaving out nonessential personal information, and it publishes a page on redacting personal information.

Does every Kansas City address record in Jackson County?

Not every one. Kansas City is the county's largest city and a co-seat, but its limits also reach into Platte and Clay counties and a small part of Cass County. A parcel north of the Missouri River can belong to a neighboring county's recorder, so check the county on the tax bill before you send a deed here.

Inside Jackson County, the same Independence office records deeds for Lee's Summit, Blue Springs, Raytown, Grandview, Grain Valley, Oak Grove, Lone Jack and the other cities. Lee's Summit alone is described by the county as home to more than 86,000 residents, so volume at one office is high. Submit complete packets, with the first-page information in place, and you reduce the odds of a return.

For an estate sale or a deed from a trust, the recorder will check only format, so sort out authority to sign with the attorney or title agent before the packet leaves your hands. Ask your title company whether it files electronically, since the county page says title firms and law offices use that portal.

How do I guard against deed fraud in Jackson County?

The recorder links an alert service at propertyfraudalert.com. Owners who sign up get a notice whenever a document is recorded against a property they own. A seller who plans to keep other parcels, or an heir managing an inherited home, can watch for a forged deed that way.

The recorder's page also links a document search for county records, and certified copies of anything found there are ordered through the Aumentum portal.

What else should a Jackson County seller check before closing?

Tax is the common loose end. The Department of Collection explains that an unpaid real estate balance follows the parcel to the buyer, so have the title agent confirm what is owed before the deed is filed. A military discharge recorded here is free, and a copy request needs a notarized form.

Census figures for 2020 to 2024 show that 59.1% of county households own and that the middle owned home is valued at $230,500, so the typical deed here conveys real money. For tax questions, see the county's property tax guide on this site, and call the Assessment office to update the owner and mailing address after a sale.

More questions about Jackson County, MO Recorder of Deeds

What will the Jackson County recorder charge me for a deed?

It charges $23 for page one and $3 for each page after. The schedule applies to documents received on or after August 28, 2026. Paying by card adds 2.75% on the whole transaction.

Is there a Kansas City counter for deed recording?

No. The county states the Recorder of Deeds is located only at the Historic Truman Courthouse, 112 W. Lexington, Suite 30, Independence, MO 64050. Mail works too, and title companies can e-record.

Will the recorder prepare my deed?

No. The office reviews and indexes documents but will not complete forms or check them beyond the minimum recording requirements. A title agent or Missouri attorney can draft it.

What if my Jackson County deed breaks the format rules?

The recorder can reject it and return it with a reason, or record it for an extra $25 under Missouri statute 59.310. Fix margins, type size and first-page details to avoid either outcome.

Where can I order a certified deed copy from Jackson County?

Order it online through the county's Aumentum portal at aumentumweb.jacksongov.org. The fee page lists $1 for certification and $2 for the first copied page plus $1 for each additional page.

Jasper County by the numbers

How do I reach the Jasper County, MO Recorder of Deeds?

The elected Recorder of Deeds is Charlotte Pickering. Call 417-358-0431 or write to recorder@jaspercounty.org. Mail goes to P.O. Box 387, Carthage, MO 64836. The office posts recording hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Central, Monday through Friday, except county holidays, which is a half hour earlier close than the 4:30 p.m. hours listed for the Carthage and Joplin county buildings.

Carthage is the county seat, and county offices there use 302 South Main Street. Joplin has its own county courts building at 633 South Pearl Avenue, yet the recorder's page lists only the Carthage mailing box, so send deeds there or ask by phone before you travel.

What does a Jasper County recorder do for a seller?

The recorder keeps the public land record for the county. Your deed to a buyer, a lender's release after payoff, and any lien notice all become effective against the world once they are recorded here.

For an inherited house, any court paper that moves title is also recorded here, and a later buyer's title search will look at this office. Ask your title agent for the recorded book and page, or the document number, once the deed is filed, and keep it with your closing papers.

How do I search Jasper County deeds online?

Go to jaspermo.icounty.com and sign in with the username guest. The guest view lets you search the index. To view and print document images, you need a subscription, which the office lists at $200 per month, or you can ask the recorder for copies.

  1. Open jaspermo.icounty.com.
  2. Enter guest as the username.
  3. Search by name or document details.
  4. Request images by subscription or from the office.

The recorder also describes a fraud alert tool inside the same system. After signing in, click your user name, choose the iRecordWeb Notification Service Settings, add the criteria you want watched, and the email on your account is notified whenever a matching document is recorded.

What changed in Jasper County recording fees on August 28, 2026?

A flat $2.00 statutory increase took effect statewide on that date for recording documents, marriage licenses and land surveys or plats. The Recorders Association of Missouri and each county recorder implemented the change under Senate Bill 938. Documents recorded before the change carried the older amount, and anything recorded now carries the higher amount.

Jasper County, MO recorder facts from the county page

Statewide fee changeFlat $2.00 increase, effective August 28, 2026

Recording hours8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday to Friday

For page-by-page pricing, the county tells people to contact the Recorder of Deeds directly. Ask for the total on your specific deed before you mail a check.

Does every Joplin address record in Jasper County?

No. Joplin is the county's largest city, yet a small part of it lies in Newton County, so a parcel in that part is recorded with the Newton County recorder. Check the county named on your tax statement or deed before mailing anything to Carthage.

The rest of Jasper County's cities all record here, including Carthage, Webb City, Carl Junction, Oronogo, Sarcoxie, Purcell, Neck City, Duenweg, Asbury, Alba and Reeds. The county adjoins Newton, Lawrence, Dade and Barton counties in Missouri, so a seller who owns land near a county line should confirm which side the legal description falls on.

What does Missouri law say about recorder fees and deed format?

Section 59.310 of the Missouri statutes lets a recorder charge $5 for the first page of a deed and $3 for each later page as the base statutory fee, plus other charges for copies, certificates and plats. A recorder may refuse a document that fails the format rules, which are in the same section.

  • Pages are printed on one side, not bound, and use dark ink with type of at least eight-point size.
  • Paper is white or light colored and at least twenty-pound weight.
  • The top margin is three inches, and the other margins are at least three-quarters of an inch.
  • Signatures have the printed name beneath them.

Copies of recorded instruments are capped at two dollars for the first page and one dollar for each page after, except plats and surveys, and a certificate and seal costs one dollar when it is not part of a recording. A nonconforming document may still be recorded for an added $25. Documents signed before 2002, military separation papers and certified copies are among those exempt from the format rules.

What must page one of a Jasper County deed show?

Below the three-inch margin, page one should state the document's title and date, every grantor and the grantor's marital status, every grantee, any statutory addresses, and the legal description of the land. If room runs out, name the page where the rest appears. Reference book and page numbers go there as well when the statute calls for them.

If the recorder rejects a document, the office must return it with the reason. Check the legal description against the prior deed in the online index before you sign, since a mismatch between old and new descriptions is the sort of problem a title agent will raise anyway.

Which other Jasper County offices matter in a home sale?

The county was organized in 1841 and named for William Jasper, a hero of the Revolutionary War, and its government is divided among separately elected officers. Three of them touch most house sales, and each has its own phone line.

  • Recorder of Deeds, Charlotte Pickering: deeds, releases and liens, 417-358-0431.
  • Collector, Steven E. McIntosh: tax statements and payment, 417-358-0411 for real property in Carthage or 417-625-4324 in Joplin.
  • Assessor, Lisa Perry: parcel values and mailing addresses, 417-358-0440.

After any sale, also ask the Assessor and Collector whether they need the new owner's mailing address so the next tax statement reaches the right person.

What else should a Jasper County seller line up before closing?

Taxes are the other half of a clean transfer. The Collector at jaspercountycollector.com sends statements in early November that are due on receipt and delinquent after December 31. See the county tax guide on this site for offices, payment methods and dates, and ask the Assessor to update the owner's mailing address after the sale.

The Census Bureau lists 127,428 residents for July 1, 2025 and 56,504 housing units, with a median owner-occupied value of $166,900 for 2020 to 2024.

More questions about Jasper County, MO Recorder of Deeds

Where do I record a deed in Jasper County, Missouri?

With the Recorder of Deeds, mailing address P.O. Box 387, Carthage, MO 64836, phone 417-358-0431. Hours are 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday through Friday.

How much does the Jasper County recorder charge to record a deed?

The office quotes page-by-page pricing on request. A flat $2.00 statutory increase took effect August 28, 2026 under Missouri SB 938. Call 417-358-0431 for the exact total on your deed.

Can I search Jasper County land records from home?

Yes. Sign in at jaspermo.icounty.com as guest to search the index. Viewing and printing images needs a $200 per month subscription, or you can ask the recorder for copies.

What happens if my deed breaks the formatting rules?

The recorder can refuse it and return it with an explanation, or record it for an extra $25 under Missouri statute 59.310. Fix the margins, type size and first-page information first.

How do I get alerts if someone records a document against my property?

Sign on at jaspermo.icounty.com, open iRecordWeb Notification Service Settings from your user name, and add your name or parcel as criteria. The email on the account is notified of each matching recording.

Selling in Jefferson County?

Get My Cash Offer →

What we could not confirm

  • Jefferson-specific appeal deadline

Jefferson County by the numbers

What does the Jefferson County Recorder of Deeds do?

The office keeps the public record of land transfers and ownership in Jefferson County, Missouri. It records deeds, deeds of trust, releases, easements, plats, restrictions, surveys and affidavits, and it issues marriage licenses (county page). Veterans' discharge papers (DD214) and tax liens can also be recorded on request.

  • Address: 729 Maple Street, Hillsboro, MO 63050.
  • Phone: 636-797-5414.
  • Cutoff: documents presented after 4:30 PM are held for processing on the next business day.
  • Rule: a document must be recorded in the county where the property sits. A Jefferson County office cannot record land in another county.

The office does not draft documents, supply blank forms or notarize the papers it records. The staff point owners to a title company or real estate attorney for that.

What does a deed need before the Jefferson County recorder will accept it?

The recorder follows section 59.310 of the Missouri statutes, which the county reprints on its recording requirements page. A document can be refused if it misses any of these points.

  • Pages printed on one side, not bound, on white or light paper of at least 20 pound weight, with type no smaller than 8 point in dark ink.
  • A blank top margin of 3 inches on page one for the recorder's stamp, and at least three-fourths of an inch on every other side.
  • On the first page below the margin: title, date, grantor names with marital status, grantee names, any statutory addresses, the legal description and any reference book and page.
  • A legal description such as lot, block and plat, or metes and bounds. A street address is never accepted as a legal description.
  • A notary acknowledgment with seal and signature, and a mailing address for at least one grantee.

A document that fails the format rules can still be recorded for an extra $25. Exempt categories include papers signed before January 1, 2002, military separation papers, documents signed outside the United States, certified copies and court judgments.

One Jefferson-specific step catches sellers of acreage. When the legal description covers less than 10 acres in an unincorporated area, or part of a lot in a subdivision, the county Planning and Zoning Department must exempt the transfer deed before the recorder will take it.

How much does it cost to record or copy a document in Jefferson County?

The state legislature sets recording fees, and the office prices a document by its page count. Fees must be paid before recording, by cash or by a check payable to the Jefferson County Recorder of Deeds. The county links a Real Estate Recording Fees PDF from its recorder quick links, so ask the office or your title company for the figure on your deed.

Recorder charges listed on Jefferson County pages
ItemCharge
Copy of a recorded document$2 first page, $1 each added page
Certification of a copy$1
Deed that fails the format rules$25 extra
Pay-per-search online records site$8.95 per search, $1 per page copied

Card orders by phone add a $1 processing fee from the card company plus postage. The county notes that part of every fee goes to the State Land Survey Office, which uses it to update state surveys and keep vital land records. That office also oversees registered surveyors.

What are the steps once a deed reaches the recorder?

The county describes a six-step path. Knowing it helps you judge why a closing package sometimes takes a day or two to come back.

  1. Staff check dates, signatures, name spellings and the acknowledgment.
  2. The document is accepted and priced by page count.
  3. It is stamped with date and time, given a document number and sealed on page one.
  4. It is scanned.
  5. It is indexed by grantor and grantee name.
  6. A second check confirms the index entry, and the document goes back to the address given. A self-addressed envelope speeds that return.

If a deed is rejected, the preparer gets it back with the reason. A deed being re-recorded must be re-acknowledged and must state why it is being re-recorded.

Which deed fits my Jefferson County sale or transfer?

The recorder's FAQ separates three common types. A warranty deed passes title to a buyer, with the seller promising the title carries no liens from the seller or earlier owners. A quit claim deed lets current owners add or remove an owner, change a name or fix an error. A beneficiary deed, also called a time of death deed, records the owner's intent for after death.

A deed of trust is the mortgage lien. Each new loan or refinance records a new one, and when it is paid the lender must record a deed of release that cites the original document number. A seller with an old, unreleased lien should ask the lender for that release before closing.

The recorder advises hiring an attorney or title company for any deed, and adds that an owner can make their own deed if it meets Missouri's formatting rules.

How do I search Jefferson County land records?

You can search in person at the vault index, which lists grantor (seller) and grantee (buyer) names alphabetically. Search your own name as grantee to find the deed from your purchase, then use the book and page number it gives. Online, the office points to a pay-per-search site, a Laredo subscription for records from April 1985 to the present, and the hosted COTT Systems site for older records.

Laredo needs a signed user agreement from the Recorder. A lost deed does not cancel ownership, since the recording is the primary evidence of title and a certified copy stands in for the original.

The county's recorder quick links also carry a Property Fraud Alert notice, a reasonable stop for any owner of a paid-off house who is approached about a deed transfer.

What is the Jefferson County housing base behind the recordings?

The Census Bureau lists 96,228 housing units and 88,309 households in Jefferson County, with about 2.58 people per household. The share of persons living in the same house a year earlier is 90.1%, a sign of long tenure (QuickFacts). Building permits totaled 617 in 2025, so new construction deeds enter the record steadily beside resales.

A sale of a house here often produces three recordings in a row: the seller's deed of release for the old loan, the warranty deed to the buyer and the buyer's new deed of trust. The office checks, prices by page count and indexes each document on its own, so a closing with several documents adds several entries to the grantor and grantee index. Ask your title company which documents it will present and in what order.

Communities that file documents here include Arnold, Festus, De Soto, Crystal City, Pevely, Herculaneum, Hillsboro and Byrnes Mill, with Eureka mostly on the St. Louis County side.

More questions about Jefferson County, MO Recorder of Deeds

Where do I record a deed in Jefferson County, Missouri?

At the Recorder of Deeds office, 729 Maple Street, Hillsboro. Call 636-797-5414 first. Anything handed in after 4:30 PM waits until the next business day.

Can the recorder write my deed for me?

No. The office cannot prepare documents or give legal advice, does not hand out blank forms and does not notarize papers it records. A title company or attorney handles that.

Is a street address enough for the legal description?

No. Section 59.310 requires a lot, block and plat, or a metes and bounds or section, township and range description. The address alone is not accepted.

What does a certified copy of my deed cost?

The county lists $2 for the first page and $1 for each added page, plus $1 to certify. A phone order by card carries a $1 card fee and postage.

Do I need planning approval before recording a deed for a small parcel?

Sometimes. A deed for under 10 acres in an unincorporated area, or part of a subdivision lot, needs a Planning and Zoning exemption before the recorder will take it.
